text:
alex: Weird one — I started `redwoodctl login`, got the browser flow, then the app auto-updated while I was in the browser. After completing auth, `redwoodctl whoami` returned unauthenticated.
nirav: hmm, auto-update kicked in mid-login? What does `redwoodctl profiles list` show?
alex: two profiles. One points to ~/.redwood (the new install) and one to ~/.redwood.old-<timestamp>. The token ended up in the .old dir.
sam: oh no. So updater replaced the binary and moved the old config dir to `.old-...` (we do that on rollback), but the login callback wrote to whichever process was active during the redirect. If the redirect hit the old process or callback helper, token landed in the moved dir.
liz: that's nasty for onboarding. New hires hit this when the updater runs automatically. We should never mutate config paths mid-login.
update-bot: update: auto-update telemetry: last_update=3312345600 user_initiated=false channel=stable
nirav: short term: block auto-update when an interactive login is in progress. Long term: make callback write to a canonical, atomic profile path (e.g., ~/.redwood/.inflight-<uuid>) and then move atomically into persistent profile after validation.
sam: Also add a lockfile around profile mutation. If updater tries to move config while the login flow holds the lock, fail update with a clear message and reschedule.
alex: can we detect this specific case retroactively and offer to migrate the token from `.old-...` back to the active profile? Might save a bunch of support tickets.
nirav: yes — add `redwoodctl migrate --from <path> --to default --preserve-backup` which will validate token freshness, copy it to the live profile, and optionally delete the backup. We'll also surface a CLI warning if we detect tokens exist in any `*.old-*` dirs.
liz: docs: add a short blurb under troubleshooting "I completed the browser flow but redwoodctl shows unauthenticated" with steps: run `profiles list --json`, check for `.old-*` dirs, run `migrate` if present, or restore backup. Also add a note to the Quickstart: disable auto-update during onboarding or run the installer manually.
sam: tests: add an integration that simulates an update during login: start login server, trigger update flow that renames config to .old-*, complete browser auth, then confirm migrate recovers token. Add unit for lockfile semantics.
update-bot: deploy queued: branch/fix/autoupdate-login-lock -> staging (CI queued).
nirav: telemetry: emit event `autoupdate.interrupt_login=true` when we detect updater moved config while an inflight login UUID is present. This helps quantify impact.
alex: small UX: if we detect tokens in `.old-*` after an update, print a one-line hint after `login` completes: "Detected tokens in backup dir .redwood.old-... Run `redwoodctl migrate --from <path> --to default` to recover."
liz: also add a support playbook entry so L1 can `profiles list` and run migrate for the user.
sam: security note: ensure migration validates token by calling `whoami` after copy before removing old copy. Keep backups for a short retention.
alex: confirmed migration command recovered my session on staging. Thanks!
